FOREWORD

0.1This

Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Institution on 26 September 1983, after the draft finalized by and Wood Products Containers Sectional Committee had been Cargo Movement and Packaging Division by the Marine, bulk for precauSuch for easy `netting'

0.2 The current indigenous practices for packing tobacoo in export include packing it in a plywood case taking all necessary tions that it withstands the hazards encountered in transportation. cases are required to be so constructed that they are amenable opening, with the cake of tobacco left intact inside the case, for purposes.

0.3 Two types of packing, namely, wooden cases and jute gunny or hessian bales are recommended in IS : 4698-1968". This standard covers the requirements for packing in plywood cases. 0.4 This standard was first published in 1976. It has been revised to In the revised version, the bring it in line with current trade-practices. moisture content of battens has been reduced from 18 to 15 percent. In the packing clause, provision has been made to use any suitable liner The clause for strapping of instead of only high density polyethylene. the box has also been suitably modified in accordance with the prevailing practices. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded of in accordance with IS : 2-19601_. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Code of practice for seaworthy packing of unmanufactured tRules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). cigarette type tobacco.

IS : 7992 - 1983 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes packing tobacco for export. 2. TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definition in addition to those given in IS : 707-1976*, and IS : 6703-19727 shall apply. 2.1 Objectionable Knots - A live knot in a batten shall be considered objectionable if its diameter along the major axis exceeds one-third of the width of the batten; provided such knots do not reach the edge of the batten and are not more than one per 30 cm length of the batten or are situated within 25 mm from a place through which a nail will be driven. 3. DIMENSIONS 3.1 The dimensions of a typical case are as follows ( see Fig. 1 and 2 ), or shall be as agreed to between the purchaser and supplier:

4.1 Plywood - Plywood used for the fabrication of the case shall conform to the requirements of Type BC, WWR Grade of ISf: 303-1975x. The minimum thickness of the plywood shall be 6 mm.

Battens

4.2.1 Battens shall be manufactured from any of the timber species given under Group I, 11 or III of Appendix A of IS : 6662-1980s.

CONSTRUCTION 5.1 Components 5.1.1 Top and Bottom Shooks .- -The top and bottom shooks shall be 1 200 x 750 mm fixed with two battens of made from 5-pIy panels 737.5 x 25 x 25 mm mitred on both ends as shown in Fig. 2. 5.1.2 Side Shooks - Two side shooks shall be made from 5-pIy panels 1 200 x 737.5 mm fixed with two 737'5 x 25 x 25 mm battens mitred on both ends as shown in Fig. 2. 5.1.3 End Shooks - End shooks shall be made from 5-ply panels 737.5 x 737.5 mm fixed with four battens comprising two battens of 687.5 x 25 x 25 mm and rest two battens of 637.5 x 25 x 25 mm as shown in Fig. 2. 5.2 Each batten shall be fixed with 14 to 16 nails as recommended to the plywood panels as shown in Fig. 1. 5.3 Make in Fig. 2. 6 mm dia grooves on all battens in 4.3

6.1 After assembling the case as in 5.4, a suitable liner, as agreed to between the purchaser and the seller shall be placed against all the interior walls of the packing case. Spread the tobacco in layers one upon the Press the strips firmly from other in the case lined with suitable liner. one to the other end of the case by using a thick wooden plank. A net mass of approximately 200 kg of tobacco may be packed in the typical case of the dimensions mentioned ,in 3.1 by an alternate process of filling and pressing with wooden plank.
NOTE For a detailed procedure for packing, see 2.2 of IS : 469%1968*.

7. CLOSING

THE BOX

7.1 After filling the tobacco, fold the liner. The box shall be closed with the top shook as prepared in 5.1.1. The case shall be sealed with the 4 aluminium wires of suitable length as shown in Fig. 1. *Code of practice for seaworthy packing of unmanufactured 7
cigarette type tobacco.

IS : 7992 - 1983
7.1.1 The plywood case shall be further wound by three or four gerrard or aluminium wires. The wire shall be suitably secured. 8. MARKING 8.1 The plywood case shall be marked at least on two opposite sides with indelible ink with the following particulars: a) Name or trade-mark b) Port of destination; c) Customer's grade; d) Serial number of the package; e) Gross mass, tare and net mass of the package; and f) Any other information required byt he buyer and by the law in force of the concerned countries. 8.1.1 The case may also be marked with any handling instructions in accordance with IS : 1260 ( Part 2 l-1979*. 8.1.2 The case may also be marked with the IS1 Certification Mark. of the manufacturer of tobacco;

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The ISI Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by JSI and operated by the producer. IS1 marked products are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.
